commitResults.messageTitle: Project: Rename Duke to King across the project
commitResults.messageBody:
The project still carries the Duke name from the original template: the
main class, both README titles, and the ASCII art banner all reference
Duke, which does not match the project's new identity.

The rename must be consistent so that code, documentation, and the
greeting shown to users all agree on the product name.

Let's,
* rename Duke.java to King.java and update the class and banner to King
* update README.md and docs/README.md titles and references from Duke
  to King

Keeping the banner, class name, and documentation in sync prevents
confusion between what the user sees and what the docs describe.

commitResults.messageTitle: King.java: Greet the user and exit
commitResults.messageBody:
The chatbot only prints its banner and terminates, so a user who runs
the program sees no greeting or farewell.

Level 0 requires the chatbot to greet the user and then exit, so the
initial program needs a proper welcome and goodbye.

Let's,
* print a greeting introducing the chatbot in King's regal tone
* ask the user what they need
* print a farewell message before the program exits
* frame the greeting and farewell with separator lines
* add Javadoc explaining the class and the LINE constant

Using a LINE constant for the separator line keeps main() readable
instead of repeating the same underscore literal several times.

commitResults.messageTitle: King: Echo user commands and exit on bye
commitResults.messageBody:
The chatbot prints its banner and farewell in one go, so the user
cannot interact with King at all.

The chatbot should read commands in a loop and respond to them.

Let's,
* read commands in a loop with a Scanner
* echo each command back to the user
* exit the loop when the user types "bye"
* add a commit message guide for the project

commitResults.messageTitle: merge level 1 feature with develop
King.java: Add item storage and list command
commitResults.messageBody:
The chatbot currently echoes every command back to the user, so it
cannot remember or show what the user has said.

Level 2 requires King to store free-form text as items and print them
on demand, so the user can build up and review a list.

Let's,
* store any non-command input as an item and confirm it with "added: ..."
* handle the "list" command by printing all stored items, numbered
* cap storage at 100 items, as the spec guarantees no more will be added
* update the class Javadoc to describe the new behavior

A fixed-size array is sufficient because the spec guarantees at most
100 items, so a dynamic collection would be unnecessary complexity.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'feature/Level-2-Add-List' into develop
King: Add mark/unmark commands and Task class
commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks are stored as plain strings, so King cannot tell whether a task
is done, and the Level 3 feature requires toggling and displaying a
done state per task.

Let's,
* introduce a Task class holding a description and an isDone flag
* replace the String[] storage with a Task[] in King
* add mark and unmark commands that toggle a task's done state
* show an [X] or [ ] status icon next to each task in the list
* print a friendly error for missing or out-of-range task indices

Modeling each task as an object keeps the done state bound to the task
itself, which the Level 3 spec's A-Classes extension asks for.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'feature/Level-3-Mark-As-Done' into develop
Docs: Polish Javadoc in King and Task
commitResults.messageBody:
- Add the missing Javadoc comment for King#main
- Append trailing periods to all @param and @return tag descriptions
  in King and Task, per the SE-EDU Java coding standard
- Re-align the updateTaskStatus parameter list to match

No behavior change; documentation and formatting only.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'refactor/A-Coding-Standard' into develop
Merge branch 'develop'
Feat: Add ToDos, Events, and Deadlines without inheritance
Refactor: Introduce Task hierarchy for ToDo, Deadline, and Event
commitResults.messageBody:
Introduce the A-Inheritance extension for Level 4.

Why:
- The no-inheritance version duplicated description, isDone, and the
  mark/unmark/status-icon logic across all three task types, and King
  had to instanceof-dispatch for every shared operation.
- A Task base class with getTaskType/getDescription/getStatusIcon lets
  King store Task[] and rely on polymorphism instead, so adding a new
  task type later requires no changes to King.

Changes:
- Task: base class holding description/isDone with markAsDone,
  markAsNotDone, getStatusIcon, getDescription, and getTaskType ("T").
- ToDo: extends Task and inherits all behavior unchanged.
- Deadline/Event: extend Task, keep only their own fields, and override
  getDescription (appending the by/from-to clauses) and getTaskType
  ("D"/"E").
- King: Task[] storage; printTask calls the task's own methods, removing
  the instanceof dispatch and the markTaskAsDone/markTaskAsNotDone
  helper methods.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'feature/Level-4-ToDos-Events-Deadlines' into develop
King: Handle invalid commands with exceptions
commitResults.messageBody:
King accepts unknown commands as tasks, and oversized task numbers or
a full todo list can terminate the conversation.

Users need specific feedback and a chance to correct invalid input.

Let's,
* introduce KingException for recoverable command errors
* validate task fields, clause markers, indices, and list capacity
* catch command errors in the input loop and exit cleanly at EOF

Parsing before mutation keeps rejected commands from changing tasks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tests: Cover Level-5 error recovery
commitResults.messageBody:
Command validation needs regression coverage to protect task state and
keep valid Level-4 commands working after an error.

Let's,
* exercise invalid fields, indices, commands, and full-list boundaries
* verify recovery, valid commands, and clean end-of-input handling
* document the command syntax and Java 25 test commands

A standard-library test harness suits the project without adding a
build framework. All eight regression tests pass with Java 25.

commitResults.messageBody:
Master needs the completed Level-5 increment and its Level-4 task types.
The course requires a separate merge commit for the increment tag.

Let's,

* include regression tests and instructions for Java 25

Preserve the feature branch and use this merge commit for Level-5.

commitResults.messageTitle: Refactor: Organize King into packages
commitResults.messageBody:
All chatbot classes share the default package, which does not express
their roles or provide a project namespace.

Let's,
* place the entry point and its tests in the king package
* group task classes in king.task and errors in king.exception
* add explicit imports while retaining the existing source roots

Grouping classes by role makes related code easier to locate. All eight
regression tests and a packaged entry-point smoke test pass on Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: Docs: Update commands for packaged classes
commitResults.messageBody:
The setup and test instructions reference default-package classes and
only search the top level of the Java source folder.

Let's,
* document the package layout and updated entry-point path
* discover Java source files recursively when compiling
* launch king.King and king.KingTest by their qualified names

These instructions keep command-line and IDE setup aligned with the
package structure while preserving src/main/java as the source root.

commitResults.messageTitle: King: Merge A-Packages increment
commitResults.messageBody:
The package organization increment is ready to join master.

Let's,
* merge the package moves and updated run instructions
* preserve a separate merge commit for the A-Packages tag

Retain branch-A-Packages for the course increment history.

commitResults.messageTitle: King: Delete tasks using a dynamic collection
commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks cannot be removed and the fixed array limits the list to 100.

Let's,
* replace the array and manual count with an ArrayList
* add deletion with confirmation and automatic renumbering
* share task-number validation across mark, unmark, and delete

The collection handles resizing and removal while invalid indices leave
the list unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tests: Cover deletion and collection growth
commitResults.messageBody:
Deletion must preserve the remaining tasks and reject invalid numbers.

Let's,
* cover removal at every position and recovery after invalid input
* verify lists can grow beyond the former 100-task limit
* document deletion and the A-Collections extension

All ten command regression tests pass with Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: Storage: Save and restore King tasks
commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks disappear when the chatbot closes, so users must recreate them.

Let's,
* load task records at startup and save after each task change
* use a relative portable path and create missing parent folders
* encode text fields and replace saves through a temporary file
* reject unreadable or corrupt data before accepting commands
* isolate existing command tests from personal save files

A separate storage class preserves task types and completion state.
Save failures warn that changes remain in memory and can be retried.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tests: Verify saving and restart recovery
commitResults.messageBody:
Persistence needs checks for data loss, first-run setup, and bad files.

Let's,
* verify every task type, completion status, and encoded text field
* check automatic saves and loading across chatbot sessions
* exercise missing folders, corrupt records, and storage failures
* document the format, failure behavior, and test commands

All eight command tests and seven persistence tests pass on Java 25.
Temporary files keep these checks separate from personal task data.

commitResults.messageTitle: King: Merge Level-6 deletion and collections
commitResults.messageBody:
Level-6 is complete on its independent increment branch.

Let's,
* merge deletion and dynamic task storage into master

All ten command regression tests pass on Java 25.

commitResults.messageTitle: King: Merge Level-7 saving with task deletion
commitResults.messageBody:
The parallel branches change task storage and the command loop.
Saving must work with Level-6 collections and persist deletions too.

Let's,
* resolve the merge using dynamic collections for loaded tasks
* save after add, mark, unmark, and delete commands
* verify deleted tasks stay removed across restarts
* cover loading and updating saves containing over 100 tasks

All ten command tests and eight persistence tests pass on Java 25.
Keep this separate merge commit as the Level-7 deliverable.

commitResults.messageTitle: Docs: Prepare King v0.1 release instructions
commitResults.messageBody:
Users need instructions for downloading and running the executable.

Let's,
* document Java 25 setup and the quoted java -jar command
* explain local data retention and the reproducible build scripts
* prepare release notes for the v0.1 JAR asset

Publish generated binaries through GitHub releases rather than Git.

commitResults.messageTitle: King: Merge executable JAR distribution
commitResults.messageBody:
The executable distribution passes standalone launch and persistence
checks with Java 25.

Let's,
* merge the build scripts, smoke test, and release instructions
* identify this source commit with A-Jar and v0.1

The JAR is distributed as a release asset, not a committed binary.
